added_failures_note: Derived from my own arms, because the reviewed manifest records baseline_suite null and after_suite at head only, so the reviewed run's own delta is unmeasured. I re-ran both arms in scratch trees extracted outside the reviewed worktree (copies of the head worktree; the 9 modified files reverted to base 0aad6627 for the base arm; the added test file removed). BASE 199 passed EXIT=0; HEAD 203 passed EXIT=0. The +4 is tests/test_jev_weighs_context.py; no test fails at head that passes at base, so added_failure_count is 0. The reviewed run's own gate-base.log (199 passed, BASE_EXIT=0) and gate-head.log (203 passed, EXIT=0) agree with my arms, though neither names the revision it ran at and the base arm ends BASE_EXIT= rather than EXIT=.

findings.text: done-when item 4 (evidence fragment with the distribution of estimated tokens against each lane's window and the rendered context block for one real node) was not produced: the review confirms the fragment path does not exist in the reviewed worktree, and the reviewed manifest's own checkpoint reads 'fragment not yet written' and its follow_ons repeat it. The node nonetheless declares status complete. The code and its tests (items 1-3) are delivered, so the node is a partial landing rather than a false one, but a named done-when artifact is missing.

scope deviation, disclosed by the worker: four files outside the declared write fence were edited - tests/test_picker.py, tests/test_picker_pressure.py, tests/test_picker_return_time.py and tests/test_jev_prompt_carries_what_it_weighs.py - each widened (a new required 'context' key added to the expected candidate field sets, and rendered-size bounds raised: 1500*4->1500*5, 1500->2200). The edits are minimal and are forced by adding a required candidate field, but they were made without a scope extension; per the node contract a write outside the fence needs a granted extension. No concurrent node claims these paths, so no collision occurred.

residual: _peak_input_utilisation filters the lane's passed rows by backend and time only, while recent_outcomes in the same module also filters by role, spec_level and model. The spec's item 2 asks for 'recent promoted runs on that lane' (lane level), so a backend-only filter is defensible, but the utilisation p50/p90 mixes every node role on the lane rather than the role being dispatched. Not a defect against the spec; recorded so a later reader of the block knows what population a non-null figure is drawn from.

residual: estimated_context_tokens passes authority=None to routing._context_file_inputs while the context-fit verdict passes resolution.authority, so for a node with granted paths the request-level estimate can differ from the per-candidate estimate the same node receives in its context block. The spec's item 1 permits a single once-per-pick figure, so this is within scope; it is recorded because the two figures can disagree for authority-granted nodes.

item_verdicts.call_sites: three: dispatch sets PickRequest.estimated_context once per pick; candidates measures the node estimate once per pick and reuses the per-backend verdict measurement through the _fit context_out out-parameter
item_verdicts.diff: read against base 0aad6627: single commit 10fca437 touches exactly the 10 files the manifest names (5 source/test in scope, 4 out-of-scope test files, 1 added test module); git diff --name-status lists those 10 and nothing else

item_verdicts.goal: Jev must weigh context: a node whose estimate approaches or exceeds a lane's window goes to a lane that fits it, and the router can choose an external lane when the local lane cannot hold the node
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, head 10fca437, base 0aad6627 (orientation), after_suite at head 0 failures, baseline_suite null; negative_control_log declared; commit body present and conventional

justifications.durability: the tests pin the behaviour as a class, not one path: CONTEXT_KEYS fixes the exact key set so a dropped field fails, headroom is asserted at ~15% for an 85%-of-window node, the unbounded-window case is asserted to render null (not zero), and the rendered state is parsed as JSON and checked on every candidate. I reproduced the declared negative control independently by forcing estimated_context to 0 on the dispatch path in a scratch copy of head: 1 failed (test_dispatch_pick_carries_a_non_zero_estimated_context), 3 passed, EXIT=1 - exactly the id the head arm passes. Residual: the single mutation exercises only the dispatch estimate; the block's own rendering guards are set by the fixtures rather than by that mutation.
justifications.evidence: the branch's declared gate is the picker, prompt, context and dispatch-speed tests plus the new module. I re-ran both arms in scratch trees outside the reviewed worktree, each header naming revision, tree, module.__file__ and cwd: HEAD 10fca437 203 passed EXIT=0; BASE 0aad6627 199 passed EXIT=0. The +4 is the new test module; zero added failures. The reviewed manifest stores baseline_suite null, so its own delta is unmeasured; I supplied the base negative above rather than a fabricated zero. The declared negative control reproduced independently.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's idiom: context joins the Candidate dataclass beside the other optional facts, the glossary and the candidate-state mapping gain one entry each, and the questions template names the block in the same sliding-scale language the file already uses. Comments state the mechanism (the estimate is advisory; a null figure is unknown, never zero) with no plan, ticket, gate or version identifier and no attribution. Symbol names describe what they measure.
justifications.goal_fidelity: items 1-3 of the done-when are delivered and independently reproduced via the head gate (203 passed, EXIT=0): dispatch sets PickRequest.estimated_context (dispatch.py:5135-5168), each offered candidate carries the context block (snapshot.py:487-500, types.py:37, prompts.py:135), and the four scenarios the spec names are asserted in tests/test_jev_weighs_context.py. Item 4, the evidence fragment, was not written, and the node declares complete over it; that is the deduction.
justifications.reuse: _context_block is the one builder for the three candidate population paths, and the verdict's own window measurement is handed forward through the _fit context_out out-parameter rather than measured a second time, avoiding a second git subprocess on the pick's critical path. No new dependency and no parallel helper were added. The node estimate is measured once per pick and reused as the no-window fallback.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status 0aad6627..10fca437 lists exactly 10 files; 5 are inside the fence and 4 (tests/test_picker.py, tests/test_picker_pressure.py, tests/test_picker_return_time.py, tests/test_jev_prompt_carries_what_it_weighs.py) are not, and the fragment/figures the fence names were not produced. The out-of-scope edits are minimal, forced by adding a required candidate field, and disclosed in the manifest's follow_ons, but they were made without a scope extension. Head is a clean descendant of base; no unrelated commits.
